surprise.title: 98 years ago today, Mickey Mouse whistled his way onto the big screen
surprise.body: On November 18, 1928, Steamboat Willie premiered at Universal's Colony Theater in New York, playing five times a day for two weeks ahead of a feature called Gang War, which has since become a lost film. It counts as Mickey and Minnie's official debut and was one of the first cartoons with fully synchronized sound, kept on the beat with a click track. The first attempt to sync the soundtrack, on September 15, 1928, was a disaster, so Walt Disney sold his Moon roadster to pay for a second recording, which worked once a bouncing ball was filmed in to hold the tempo. Ub Iwerks led the animation, Disney voiced every character himself, and the whole short cost $4,986.69. Steamboat Willie entered the U.S. public domain on January 1, 2024, and its whistling-at-the-wheel clip still opens every Walt Disney Animation Studios film. Fitting ship lore, too, with 25 days until you sail on December 13. Tallahassee runs about 54°F this morning, climbing near 69°F as the clouds break around midday, with sunset at 5:38 PM.
